issue.title: Proper way to build with superbuild off?
issue.body:
Hi,

When I try to build MAVSDK with superbuild off, from v3.8.0 I get this message:
gmake[2]: *** No rule to make target 'third_party/install/include/mavlink/message_definitions/v1.0/ardupilotmega.xml', needed by 'src/mavsdk/core/embedded_mavlink_xml.h'.  Stop.
It makes sense since this one, and the others, are not there.

I read your discussion @julianoes and @JonasVautherin when the MavlinkDirect plugin was first added, but could not find a way how to point to a different location. All I see are the hard-coded set(MAVLINK_MINIMAL_XML... in the CMakeLists.txt and when I change these to point to my location, MAVSDK is built properly.

If, like @JonasVautherin suggested, there is a way to specify this location via a cmake flag, it would be fine I guess. Not sure how that should be done so I would like to ask you... thanks!

Update: ok, that wasn't so hard, created a PR to set the variables only when not specified

comments.body: Oops. We used to have a non-superbuild build in CI that I could have referred you to. Looks like we should add that again. And fix your issue while doing so.
no problem, it's good to dive into the code/cmake to gain some knowledge.

Here is my current work in progress to get the build to work without superbuild. There is still work to go.

```docker
FROM ubuntu:22.04

WORKDIR /ws

# https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build_linux.html

RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        git \
        python3 \
        python3-pip \ 
        liblzma-dev

RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink.git
WORKDIR /ws/mavlink
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive
RUN cmake -B build -S .
RUN cmake --build build
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install

WORKDIR /ws
RUN git clone --branch python3-executable https://github.com/ryanf55/libevents.git
WORKDIR /ws/libevents
RUN python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
RUN cmake -B build -S libs/cpp
RUN cmake --build build
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install

WORKDIR /ws
RUN git clone --branch cmake-install-support https://github.com/julianoes/PicoSHA2
WORKDIR /ws/PicoSHA2
RUN cmake -B build -S .
RUN cmake --build build
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install

WORKDIR /ws
RUN git clone https://github.com/julianoes/libmavlike
WORKDIR /ws/libmavlike
RUN git reset --hard 80dbd91a0c5d6f0a79f1e8597b820ba075d1cf15
RUN cmake -B build -S .
RUN cmake --build build
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install

WORKDIR /ws
RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/ws/mavlink/install:/ws/libevents/install:/ws/PicoSHA2/install cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S . -DSUPERBUILD=OFF -DBUILD_WITHOUT_CURL=ON 
RUN cmake --build build -j8 --target install
```
The dependencies built by the superbuild are here: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/third_party/CMakeLists.txt.
What's the status here? What else is needed?

More time to get through the rest of the dockerfile.
Because we have removed some of the patches, things are getting closer. 
Let's leave this open till I finish the Dockerfile, and then we can add it to the repo or wiki or something.

@Ryanf55 ok I want to get this wrapped up, so I continued here: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2730

I'm not using a dockerfile but just a bash script instead. Anyone can transform that into docker if required, I'd argue.

Note that instead of using a bash script, it's also possible to just reuse all the CMake scripts from https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/third_party, and just make them install somewhere locally. 

It's of course possible to rewrite the helpers in any language you like 👍. The bonus with our helpers is that they are cross-platform 😇.
Right, so I should re-use them in the example bash script.
I'm gonna merge the script as is. It's just an example for people to follow if they want to.

issue.title: Document/support process for using custom mavlink dialect

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
I want to add a few custom mavlink messages for my own dialect, not part of upstream, and develop without having to commit and push to a repository.

Right now, mavlink is brought in through ExternalProject_add like so:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt#L32-L45



The URL is hard-coded to upstream
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt#L34

Then, for a local build, mavlink is built and installed, so that its config file is on disk.
This allows it to be found through find_package:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L4

For some reason, regardless of the setting for the MAVLINK_DIALECT, it does not get affect the command here:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L27-L39


I want to

* Add a new local mavlink XML dialect, say my_custom.xml
* Get MAVSDK to also generate that dialect in addition to the normal dialect
* Use those new messages to send custom packets via mavsdk

Can we either document or add support for mavlink to be brought in through a submodule, fetchcontent, or how to build/install mavlink on the system that does not rely on merging stuff upstream first? Perhaps we can support a way where mavlink on the system can be used.

In mavlink:
```
cmake -B build -DMAVLINK_DIALECT=MyCustomDialect
cmake --build build
cmake --install build --prefix install
```
Which generates the following header (as expected)
```
/home/ryan/Dev/mavlink/install/include/mavlink/MyCustomDialect/mavlink_msg_my_custom_dialect_toy.h
```
Then, when building MAVSDK, perhaps we can allow a user to add "/path/to/mavlink/install" to the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH and use that version instead of pulling from upstream.

Trying this today results in the following error:
```
gmake[2]: *** No rule to make target 'third_party/install/include/mavlink/message_definitions/v1.0/ardupilotmega.xml', needed by 'src/mavsdk/core/embedded_mavlink_xml.h'.  Stop.
gmake[1]: *** [CMakeFiles/Makefile2:910: src/mavsdk/core/CMakeFiles/generate_core_mavlink_xml_header.dir/all] Error 2
gmake: *** [Makefile:136: all] Error 2
```
I spent a fair bit of time trying to understand this step of the build system but don't know how to proceed.
